title: Global view of domain-specific O-linked mannose glycosylation in glycoengineered cells
projectDescription: Protein O-linked mannose (O-Man) glycosylation is an evolutionary conserved post-translational modification, whose biosynthesis is initiated by three non-redundant enzyme families, POMT1/POMT2, TMTC1-4 and TMEM260. In this study, we applied a targeted workflow for membrane glycoproteomics to five human cell lines and to a panel of genetically engineered cells with individual and combinatorial knock-out of O-Man glycosyltransferase genes to extensively map substrates, specificities, and crosstalk of O-Man enzymes. Our quantitative glycoproteomics results demonstrate new protein targets for the POMT1/POMT2 pathway and show that TMTC1-4 and TMEM260 widely target distinct Ig-like protein domains of plasma membrane proteins. This new evidence adds further knowledge on the emerging concept of domain-specific O-Man glycosylation and establishes a platform for functional studies of O-Man glycosylated adhesion molecules and receptors.
sampleProcessingProtocol: This work comprises (I) complex samples shotgun glycoproteomics and (II) affinity purification (glyco)proteomics. For (I), proteins are extracted from membrane or total cell fraction and digested with workhorse proteases. Case and control cell lines are labelled with stable diethyl isotopes and mixed, before lectin chromatography for enrichment of O-Man and C-Man peptides. Samples are desalted and subjected to nLC-MS/MS on Orbitrap Tribrid Fusion/Lumos. For (II), proteins are purified from cellular supernatant or lysate before affinity purification. Purified proteins are digested with workhorse proteases on S-Trap columns (ProtiFi), labelled with stable diethyl isotopes and mixed, unless differently specified. Desalted peptide mixtures are subjected to nLC-MS/MS on Orbitrap Tribrid Fusion/Lumos.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw files are analysed using Proteome Discoverer 1.4.1.14 (Thermo). All peptide spectral matches (PSMs) are based on probability-based scoring (Sequest-HT, p<0.01) and manual inspection of glycopeptide MS/MS identifications and MS1-level quantifications to ensure the accuracy of the assignments.
